title: Conservation of energy
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:58Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point is a senior Victorian Physics card that goes beyond the Year 9 conservation idea into power (P = E ÷ t) and efficiency, and both of its questions test those skills rather than conservation, so it is broader and at a different depth.

draft.title: Conservation of energy
card: Energy cannot be made or destroyed. It can only be transferred from one object to another, or transformed from one type to another.
energy moves from one place or object to another, such as heat moving from a hot drink into a cold cup.
energy changes type, such as chemical energy in a battery becoming electrical energy and then light and heat.
The total energy in a system stays the same before and after. Some energy often ends up as heat or sound that spreads into the surroundings, so it is hard to collect, but it has not disappeared.
draft.remember: Energy is never lost or created. The total stays the same, even when it spreads out.

a.q: A ball rolls along a rough floor and slows to a stop. What happens to its kinetic energy?
opts: It becomes heat and sound in the floor and air
It is destroyed because the ball has stopped
It stays in the ball as kinetic energy
It becomes new energy that adds to the total
a.why: Energy is not destroyed. The ball's kinetic energy is transformed into heat and sound, which spread into the floor and air. Saying it is destroyed is tempting because the ball stops moving, but the energy has only changed form.
a.clue: Where does the energy go if it cannot disappear?

b.q: Priya's torch has a battery that stores 100 J of chemical energy. It gives out 20 J as light. How much energy goes elsewhere?
opts: 80 J, as heat in the torch and its surroundings
0 J, because the battery energy was used up
80 J, which is destroyed inside the torch
20 J, because light and heat share the energy equally
b.why: The total stays at 100 J, so 100 J minus 20 J leaves 80 J. It is transformed into heat that spreads into the torch and the air. Calling it used up or destroyed is tempting, but energy is never destroyed.
b.clue: The total energy before and after must match.

a.best: It becomes heat and sound in the floor and air

b.best: 80 J, as heat in the torch and its surroundings
